title: Boat Club vs. Owning a Boat in Illinois: Costs and Trade-Offs
author: Quest Watersports
summary_html: What does it really cost to own a boat in Illinois, and when does a boat club make more sense? A straightforward comparison from Quest Watersports.
body_html:
Almost everyone who loves the water has had the same thought: should I buy a boat, or is there an easier way? The honest answer depends on how often you will use it and how much of the work you want to do yourself.

This guide walks through the real costs of owning a boat in Illinois and how a boat club like Quest Express compares. We sell boats and run a club, so we will tell you where each one fits.

What owning a boat actually involves

The purchase price is only the start. Here are the cost categories every owner should plan for. We are not quoting prices because they vary widely by boat, so use this as a checklist for your own budget.

Loan or purchase cost

Most buyers finance. Look at the monthly payment, down payment and term. Boats also lose value over time, so depreciation is a real cost even though it never shows up on a bill.

Insurance

Boat insurance usually covers damage, theft and liability. Rates depend on boat type, value, where you keep it and your experience. Lenders often require coverage.

Registration and licensing

Powered boats are registered with the state, and trailers have their own registration. Check the current Illinois DNR requirements for your boat and for any course or certificate that applies to operators.

Storage and slip fees

Your boat needs a place to live. Options include a slip at a marina, dry storage, or a trailer at home. Off-season storage is a separate line item in Illinois, where winters are long. Our boat storage and off-season service page covers what we offer.

Winterizing and spring commissioning

In a climate that freezes, engines and water systems must be winterized every fall and prepared again in spring. Skipping it can be expensive. Many owners pay a shop to do it each year.

Maintenance and repairs

Oil, filters, impellers, batteries, upholstery, props and cleaning add up. Unexpected repairs are the wild card. Our service and parts department can handle routine work and repairs.

Trailering and towing

If you trailer your boat, you need a suitable tow vehicle, a trailer in good condition, and time for loading and launching. Trailers need maintenance too: tires, bearings and lights.

Fuel, gear and extras

Fuel, life jackets, safety equipment, dock lines, tow toys and electronics all cost money. Owners also spend time cleaning, hauling and prepping the boat before each outing.

The time cost

Money is not the only cost. Owning a boat also means hours of cleaning, hauling, launching, retrieving and winterizing. For a lot of families, the time matters more than the dollars. If you only get out a handful of times a season, the cost per day on the water can be high.

How Quest Express Boat Club works

Quest Express is a boat club based at Heritage Harbor Ottawa on the Illinois River. Instead of owning one boat, members reserve from a fleet. Here is what the club says it covers, taken from our boat club page and boat club FAQ:

  • No boat payment, licensing or insurance expense. Quest Express maintains a Club policy that covers major damage and liability.
  • No cleaning, upkeep, repairs or maintenance. Club staff handle regular maintenance and detailing.
  • No slip fees, winterizing or winter storage.
  • No daily use charges. Other than membership fees, the recurring cost is the fuel you use. Concierge services such as catering or boat guide coaching cost extra.
  • A variety of boats. Members choose from pontoons, tritoons, sport-ready boats and more, depending on the day.
  • Reservations online from 2 hours to 30 days in advance, plus a same-day option when a boat is available.

Members must be 21 or older with a valid Illinois driver's license, and no boating experience is required. Orientation covers handling the boats, launching from the marina and boating on the Illinois waterway. A membership runs 365 days, and each plan covers up to 2 members.

Trade-offs to be honest about

What a club does well

  • It removes the long list of ownership chores.
  • You can try different boat types before deciding what you like.
  • The cost is more predictable than ownership.

What a club does not do

  • It is not your boat. You cannot customize it, leave your gear aboard or be guaranteed a specific boat on a specific holiday. Quest Express says availability is excellent almost all the time, but not guaranteed.
  • Boating is limited to the Ottawa pool, between the Marseilles Lock and the Starved Rock Lock, about 14 miles. If you want to trailer to other lakes or the Great Lakes, you will want your own boat.
  • You build no equity. Owned boats can be sold. Membership payments are for use.

Who should own and who should join

Owning tends to fit if you

  • Plan to boat many times each season and in many places.
  • Want to fish, camp or cruise multi-day trips from your own boat.
  • Enjoy working on boats and customizing them.

A club tends to fit if you

  • Want a handful of great days a season, or a summer of weekends, without the chores.
  • Are new to boating and want to learn before you commit.
  • Would rather spend free time on the water than at the shop.

Try before you buy

Many people use the club as a stepping stone. Quest Express is, in our words, an excellent opportunity to learn how to handle different boats and decide whether you wish to become a boat owner. Ready to buy later? See boats for sale in Ottawa. We also take trade-ins at sell or trade your boat.

Why the Illinois River matters

Both options put you on the Illinois River at Heritage Harbor, in the heart of Starved Rock Country. The river is less crowded than many northern Illinois lakes, with scenic bluffs and islands. Learn more in our guide to boating the Illinois River.

Take the next step

Tell us how often you would boat and what you want to do, and we will help you decide. To tour the marina and the fleet, call 815.433.2200 or stop by the shop. Hear from members on the testimonials page.

FAQ

Do I need boat insurance with Quest Express?

No. Quest Express maintains a Club policy that covers major damage and liability.

Are there daily use charges?

No. The only recurring costs other than membership fees are for fuel you use. Concierge services such as catering or boat guide coaching are available for an additional fee.

Who can join Quest Express?

Anyone 21 or older with a valid Illinois driver's license. No boating experience is required, and orientation is provided.

Where can club members boat?

Use is limited to the Ottawa pool, between the Marseilles Lock and the Starved Rock Lock, about 14 miles of the Illinois River.

Is a boat club cheaper than owning a boat?

It depends on how often you boat. A club removes ownership costs such as the loan, insurance, storage, winterizing and maintenance, so many occasional boaters find it simpler and more predictable. Call us to talk through your situation and to get current membership information.
